citation.title: Adversarial Agents on Topology Optimization: Understanding the Fragility and Robustness of Deep Learning-based and Physics-Based Design Models under Adversarial Perturbation
citation.authors: Hoang Anh Nguyen, Yuan Hong, Hongyi Xu

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: On 45 held-out problems, rerunning SIMP from attacked surrogate initializations returned median compliance at 1.000 times the reference for every tested model, with 14 of 405 reruns above a 1.05 penalty.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No quantitative speed-up against a classical method is claimed for the primary outcome.
claim.alternatives: Abstract: bounded perturbations caused multi-order compliance degradation in some surrogates; unperturbed surrogate quality is described as near baseline (Section 5.1).

baseline.implementation: Article's own SIMP dataset generator and rerun implementation; code not publicly available in article
baseline.solver: Finite-element equilibrium solve; solver type not stated
baseline.quality_metric: Thresholded finite-element compliance; paired adv/clean or SIMP-rerun/GT compliance ratio
baseline.quality_gap: Median SIMP-rerun/GT ratio 1.000 × for all nine sources; 14/405 reruns exceeded 1.05 × (Section 5.4, Table 3).

R1.evidence: The coded primary outcome compares compliance quality, not speed or a matched-time comparison (Section 5.4).

R2.evidence: No primary speed comparison requiring assessment of baseline efficiency is made (Section 5.4).

R3.evidence: The coded outcome concerns compliance recovery and does not claim a measured speed advantage (Conclusion; Section 5.4).

R4.evidence: Sections 5.1–5.4 evaluate returned predictions with thresholded FE compliance and report test-set exceedance counts, but do not report constraint satisfaction for the returned designs (Tables 1–3).

notes: The authors state that data and model will be available upon email request (Appendix); no public code link or permission to run is reported. Source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.22606
